gloss: to fall deeply in love with, to be captivated by

definitions.gloss: to fall deeply in love with, to be captivated by
definitions.explanation: To become thoroughly enamored or deeply attracted to someone or something. Stronger than simple liking — implies being completely won over. Used for romantic attraction, but also for being captivated by a place, a work of art, or an idea.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}に{惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I fell head over heels for her.

examples.japanese: この{土地|とち}の{景色|けしき}に{惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}んで、{移住|いじゅう}を{決|き}めた。
examples.english: I was so captivated by the scenery here that I decided to move.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はその{脚本|きゃくほん}に{惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}み、{自|みずか}ら{監督|かんとく}を{申|もう}し{出|で}た。
examples.english: He was so taken with the screenplay that he volunteered to direct it himself.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
Godan verb (む-ending). {惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}む → {惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}まない → {惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}んだ → {惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}んで

USAGE:
{惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}む is an intensified form of {惚|ほ}れる (to fall in love with). The {込|こ}む suffix adds the sense of depth and thoroughness — being deeply and completely captivated.

Used for both romantic and non-romantic contexts. Often takes the particle に to mark the object of fascination.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～に{惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}む: to be captivated by ~
- すっかり{惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}む: to be completely smitten
- {一目|ひとめ}で{惚|ほ}れ{込|こ}む: to be captivated at first sight
